questions.stem: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. Plants and algae absorb CO2 and use it, along with water and light energy, to produce glucose and oxygen. This converts atmospheric carbon into organic compounds.

questions.stem: Which of the following processes releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Respiration (by all living organisms), combustion (burning fossil fuels and wood), and decomposition (breakdown of dead matter by microorganisms) all release CO2 into the atmosphere.

options.text: From carbon dioxide dissolving in the ocean
From rocks being weathered by rain
From the remains of ancient organisms compressed over millions of years

questions.explanation: Fossil fuels (coal, oil, and natural gas) formed from the remains of ancient organisms that were buried and compressed over millions of years. The carbon in these organisms became locked away as hydrocarbons underground.

questions.stem: Why is the carbon cycle important?

options.text: It destroys excess carbon in the atmosphere
It recycles carbon between the atmosphere, living organisms, and the Earth
It only affects plants, not animals

questions.explanation: The carbon cycle is important because it recycles carbon between different reservoirs -- the atmosphere, living organisms, oceans, and rocks. This ensures carbon is continuously available for building organic molecules essential for life.

questions.stem: How have human activities affected the carbon cycle?

options.text: By reducing the amount of CO2 in the atmosphere
Human activities have no effect on the carbon cycle
By increasing atmospheric CO2 through burning fossil fuels and deforestation

questions.explanation: Humans have increased atmospheric CO2 by burning fossil fuels (releasing stored carbon) and deforestation (removing trees that absorb CO2). This has disrupted the natural balance of the carbon cycle and contributed to climate change.

questions.stem: What role do decomposers play in the carbon cycle?

options.text: They absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
They convert carbon into fossil fuels
They break down dead organisms, releasing CO2 through respiration
They have no role in the carbon cycle

questions.explanation: Decomposers (bacteria and fungi) break down dead organisms and waste materials. During this process, they respire and release carbon dioxide back into the atmosphere, recycling the carbon that was locked in organic matter.

questions.stem: Which carbon reservoir stores the largest amount of carbon?
questions.explanation: Rocks such as limestone (calcium carbonate) store the largest amount of carbon. Although the atmosphere contains a relatively small amount of carbon, it is very important because changes in atmospheric CO2 affect global climate.
